facts: **$V = Ah$**, where $A$ is the area of the uniform cross-section and $h$ is the perpendicular distance through the prism.
The "base" of a prism is its uniform cross-section, not necessarily the face it is sitting on.
Cross-section area formulas: rectangle $A = lw$, triangle $A = \frac{bh}{2}$, parallelogram $A = bh$, trapezium $A = \frac{h(a+b)}{2}$.
Every area formula uses the **perpendicular** height of the shape, never a slant side.
Put all dimensions in the same unit before substituting.
An area in cm² multiplied by a length in cm gives a volume in cm³.
steps: Find the area of the uniform cross-section.
Substitute the cross-section area and the perpendicular height into $V = Ah$.
Evaluate and write the answer in cubic units.

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the volume of each solid in cm³.

a. A rectangular prism measures $5$ cm by $3$ cm by $8$ cm.

b. A cube has side length $4$ cm.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a. The rectangular cross-section has area $5\times3$ cm².

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(5\times3)\times8\\&=120\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

b. The cube has a square cross-section and an equal distance through it.

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(4\times4)\times4\\&=64\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

The perpendicular sides are $12$ cm and $5$ cm. The $13$ cm slant side is not the triangle's height.

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=\left(\frac{12\times5}{2}\right)\times8\\&=30\times8\\&=240\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Use the perpendicular height of the parallelogram.

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(8\times4)\times9\\&=32\times9\\&=288\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

The uniform cross-section is the trapezium-shaped side wall. Its parallel sides are the two depths, and the perpendicular distance between them is $18.6$ m. The distance through the prism is the pool's width.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{18.6(1.35+2.75)}{2}\\&=38.13\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=38.13\times6.4\\&=244.032\text{ m}^{3}\\&\approx244.03\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A school makes $40$ identical doorstops from recycled plastic. Each doorstop is a triangular prism with a right-triangle cross-section of base $6$ cm and perpendicular height $2$ cm. Each prism is $4$ cm long. Find the total volume of plastic needed in cm³.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For one doorstop:

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=\left(\frac{6\times2}{2}\right)\times4\\&=6\times4\\&=24\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

For all $40$ doorstops:

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{total}}&=40\times24\\&=960\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Two rectangular prisms have the same volume. Prism A measures $5$ cm by $4$ cm by $x$ cm. Prism B measures $8$ cm by $6$ cm by $5$ cm. Find $x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For prism B:

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(8\times6)\times5\\&=240\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Prism A has the same volume.

$\begin{aligned}(5\times4)x&=240\\20x&=240\\x&=240\div20\\x&=12\end{aligned}$

The missing length is $12$ cm.

workedExamples.question_text: A prism has a uniform cross-sectional area of $28$ cm² and a volume of $1540$ cm³. Find its length in cm.
A vase occupies $260$ cm³ inside a rectangular box with internal dimensions of $11$ cm by $8$ cm by $7$ cm. Packing foam fills the remaining space. Find the volume of foam in cm³.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For the box:

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(11\times8)\times7\\&=616\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Subtract the volume occupied by the vase.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{foam}}&=616-260\\&=356\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text:
A rectangular prism measures $4$ cm by $3$ cm by $7$ cm.
Find its volume in cm³.

The uniform cross-section of a triangular prism is a right triangle with perpendicular sides of $5$ mm and $8$ mm. The prism is $9$ mm long.
Find its volume in mm³.

A prism has a parallelogram cross-section with a base of $6$ m and a perpendicular height of $3$ m. The prism is $8$ m long.
Find its volume in m³.

foundation.solution_text:
The perpendicular height of the triangle is $8$ cm; the $10$ cm side is a slant.
$V = Ah$
$= \left(\frac{6 \times 8}{2}\right) \times 5$
$= 24 \times 5$
$= 120\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text:
A prism has a trapezium cross-section with parallel sides of $4.5$ cm and $8.5$ cm and a perpendicular height of $3.2$ cm. The prism is $7.5$ cm long.
Find its volume in cm³.

Two rectangular prisms have the same volume. Prism A measures $6$ cm by $4$ cm by $x$ cm. Prism B measures $9$ cm by $8$ cm by $5$ cm.
Find the value of $x$.
development.solution_text:
Prism B: $V = (9 \times 8) \times 5$
$= 360\text{ cm}^{3}$
Prism A: $24x = 360$
$x = 360 \div 24$
$x = 15$
The missing length is $15$ cm.

development.question_text:
A prism has a uniform cross-sectional area of $32$ cm² and a volume of $2400$ cm³.
Find the length of the prism in cm.

A triangular prism has a right-triangle cross-section with perpendicular sides of $9$ m and $12$ m and a slant side of $15$ m. The prism is $7$ m long.
Find its volume in m³.

mastery.question_text:
A swimming pool is $25$ m long and $8$ m wide.
The floor slopes evenly from $1$ m deep at the shallow end to $2.5$ m deep at the deep end, so the side wall of the pool is a trapezium.
Find the volume of water in the full pool.
Give your answer in m³.
mastery.solution_text:
The uniform cross-section is the trapezium-shaped side wall, and the width of the pool is the distance through it.
$A = \frac{25(1 + 2.5)}{2}$
$= 43.75\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 43.75 \times 8$
$= 350\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text:
A prism has a trapezium cross-section whose parallel sides are $2.75$ m and $4.65$ m, measured $1.35$ m apart. The prism is $6.4$ m long.
Find its volume in m³, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A vase with a volume of $425$ cm³ is packed into a rectangular box with internal dimensions of $12.5$ cm by $8$ cm by $9$ cm. The space around the vase is filled with packing foam.
Find the volume of foam in cm³.
